title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model Serving, Observability, Performance + ADR Index
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure IaC, model-serving patterns, observability, performance targets, and our recent decision records (ADRs). It is intended as the canonical reference for engineering teams when designing, reviewing, and operating services that interact with the inference platform.

Purpose:
- Provide a single, actionable set of conventions teams can follow to ensure interoperability, reliability, and predictable performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Document guardrails used by platform teams to create automated checks (linting, CI gates, infra policy) and onboarding materials.

Scope:
Applies to: public APIs (REST/gRPC), internal service-to-service APIs, SDKs, Terraform modules and cloud accounts, model packaging and serving configs, observability instrumentation, performance benchmarking, and ADRs that affect cross-team behavior.

Principles (applied to all areas):
1) Developer-first: APIs and conventions should minimize cognitive load and onboarding friction.
2) Production-first: prioritize observability, retries/backoff, and graceful degradation.
3) Backward-compatibility: prefer additive changes and provide migration paths.
4) Economical: expose knobs for cost/latency tradeoffs.
5) Secure by default: default to least privilege, encryption, and auditability.

Section 1 
— API Standards:
- Surface: REST+JSON for public-facing endpoints; gRPC for high-throughput internal service-to-service calls where low latency and type-safety are required.
- Base path convention: /v{major}/{service}/{resource} (example: /v1/inference/sessions). Major version increments only for breaking changes.
- Resource naming: kebab-case for HTTP URIs, camelCase for JSON properties in SDKs. Example: {"sessionId": "...", "modelName": "redwood-1.2"}.
- Versioning: use semantic versioning for model artifacts and MAJOR for API. Deprecation windows must be published at least 90 days prior to MAJOR change.
- Response envelope: all responses must include {"ok": boolean, "data": object|null, "error": object|null}. Error object: {"code": string, "message": string, "hint": string|null}.
- Pagination: use cursor-based pagination (next_cursor token) for streaming large lists.
- Rate limiting: endpoints must return X-RateLimit-*, and 429 responses must include retry_after in seconds.
- Authentication: tokens via Authorization: Bearer <token>. All public APIs require TLS 1.2+.
- Contract tests: every service must publish OpenAPI or gRPC proto and include contract tests in CI (example: contract-test.sh).

Section 2 
— Coding Standards:
- Languages: Python (inference & tooling), Go (control-plane services), TypeScript (console and SDK).
- Style & linting: use black/isort/ruff for Python; gofmt/golangci-lint for Go; eslint/prettier for TypeScript. CI gate fails on style or linter errors.
- Testing: unit coverage target >= 70% for new services; critical path libraries >= 85%. Integration tests required for networked services (mocked downstreams allowed using recorded fixtures).
- API surface and docs: every public function/class must include docstrings and be surfaced in generated docs. SDKs must include end-to-end examples.
- Dependency policy: follow minimal third-party dependency principle; security team must approve dependencies with >100k weekly downloads.

Section 3 
— Infrastructure Standards (IaC):
- Terraform: use centralized module registry. All cloud resources must be provisioned via Terraform in the canonical repo (infra/).
- Module patterns: modules must be parameterized, idempotent, and documented. Use semantic module versions.
- Tagging: all resources include tags: {"team":"<team>", "env":"<dev|staging|prod>", "service":"<service-name>"}.
- Networking: VPCs must enforce subnet separation (control plane vs data plane), ingress limited to required IP ranges, and use private endpoints for internal services.
- Secrets: use KMS + secrets manager; no plaintext secrets in repos. CI must use short-lived credentials.
- Multi-region: critical services (control plane) deployed in at least two regions with automated failover policy documented in runbooks.

Section 4 
— Model Serving Standards:
- Packaging: models must be packaged with a manifest.json including model_version, architecture, weights_hash, quantization_profile_id, and supported_seq_lengths.
- Versioning: model artifacts use semantic model_version. Serving config must include compatible runtime docker image tag and kernel profile.
- Quantization profiles: reference profiles live under /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Each profile must document measured quality delta and throughput gain.
- KV cache & prefix caching: model runtime must expose config for prefix cache TTL, max_kv_size, and eviction policy. Default TTL = 60s for short-lived sessions, configurable per-route.
- Fallbacks & routing: route by policy (latency/cost/region). Define fallback model families per workload (e.g., redwood-1 -> redwood-lite-1).
- Safety & guardrails: each model must ship with a safety filter manifest; service-level content filters must be configurable by customer tier.
- Rollouts: Canary (5%), gradual ramp (20%, 50%, 100%) with automated canary observability checks (latency, error rate, quality checks).

Section 5 
— Observability Standards:
- Metrics: use Prometheus metrics with naming prefix redwood_<service>_<metric>. Key metrics: request_count, request_errors, request_duration_seconds_bucket, tokens_consumed_total, model_cache_hit_ratio.
- Traces: use OpenTelemetry. Trace context must be propagated across service boundaries (W3C traceparent).
- Logs: structured JSON logs (timestamp, level, service, request_id, user_id?, message, extras). Sanitize PII prior to logging.
- Dashboards: per-service dashboards must include SLO panels, latency P50/P95/P99, error rates, and downstream saturation.
- SLOs & alerts: SLOs defined centrally; alerts only for actionables. Example SLOs in Appendix.
- Sampling & retention: traces sampled at 10% by default; retain metrics 13 months for trend analysis; high-cardinality logs retained 30 days unless flagged for longer retention by support.

Section 6 
— Performance Standards & Benchmarking:
- Latency targets (representative):
  - Public inference API small models: p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 800ms.
  - Large autoregressive models: p95 <= 1.5s for 512 tokens.
  - Embeddings endpoints: p95 <= 200ms.
- Throughput: dedicated pools must document expected tokens/sec per GPU profile.
- Load testing: every public service must run a load test in staging each release (k6 or Locust). Tests must include realistic prompt distributions and KV-cache warmups.
- Benchmark harness: eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite is the canonical harness. Results archived per-run with metadata: model, batch_size, seq_len, GPU_type, kernel_profile.
- Profiling: perf profiles or Nsight traces for GPU-bound services at least quarterly or after any major deployment impacting runtime.

Section 7 
— ADR Index (summary of recent decisions):
1) ADR-2025-08: Standardize public API envelopes \u2014 decision: adopt {ok,data,error} envelope; reason: consistent error handling across SDKs.
2) ADR-2025-11: Model versioning scheme \u2014 decision: separate model semantic versioning from API MAJOR to allow independent rollouts.
3) ADR-2026-01: Default to REST for public APIs, gRPC internal \u2014 decision: maintain REST for external discoverability and gRPC for performance inside cluster.
4) ADR-2026-04: Use OpenTelemetry for traces \u2014 decision: unify traces for cross-service root-cause and latency attribution.
(Full ADRs: see /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records)

Enforcement & Review:
- Ownership: Architecture Standards Board (ASB) \u2014 engineering leads across runtime, infra, API, and SRE. Board owner: Director of Platform (owner: "engineering").
- Review cadence: quarterly review of standards; ad-hoc reviews for each breaking ADR.
- CI/Automation: linting, contract tests, and Terraform plan checks implemented as required PR checks. Policy violations block merges.
- Exceptions: teams may request exceptions by filing a short RFC and approval from ASB; exceptions recorded as ADR addendums.

Appendix \u2014 Example SLO table (config snippet):
| Service | SLO Target (availability) | Latency SLO (p95) | Error Budget | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| inference-public | 99.9% | 300ms | 43.2 mins/month | inference-runtime@redwood.com |
| model-router | 99.95% | 150ms | 21.6 mins/month | model-router@redwood.com |
| control-plane-api | 99.99% | 100ms | 4.32 mins/month | control-plane@redwood.com |

How to use this doc (procedures):
1) New service onboarding: follow the checklist in eng-platform/how-tos/onboarding-checklist. Required items: OpenAPI/proto, contract tests, infra module, SLO proposal, and dashboard.
2) Changes to public API: file an ADR for breaking changes; allow 90-day deprecation window; prepare migration guide and SDK updates.
3) Model rollouts: create rollout plan in product docs, schedule canary with monitoring, and escalate on any SLO regression.
